purpose: library: the kinetic theory of gases — modelling a gas as molecules very small relative to the distance between them, in constant random motion, frequently colliding with each other and with container walls; density as the sum of molecular mass divided by volume; pressure as a measure of the molecules' linear momentum (collisions impart momentum to the walls, producing a measurable force; force divided by area is pressure); temperature as a measure of the mean kinetic energy (mass times the square of the velocity of the random motion); solid vs gas molecular behaviour; and the random vs ordered (wind) motion components, which are indistinguishable at the molecular level. Fits quiz cards with predict-then-reveal, a compare table of what density/pressure/temperature each measure molecularly, and a concept map of the theory's assumptions; pairs with the stored ideal-gas equation-of-state page.
